## High-Recall Evidence Router — Chapter 5B — MAC-010 (IMF 2022 Article IV Mexico)

I have analyzed all 104 chunks against the 10 Chapter 5B (economic wellbeing) lenses. The IMF 2022 Article IV staff report is a premier 5B source: it is authored by the Western Hemisphere Department, draws on official Mexican data, covers 2021–2023 with forward projections, and discusses the ruler's economic agenda, institutions, rules, distribution, and trajectory across all 10 lenses. Below is the complete per-chunk decision ledger.

---

### Routing Ledger

| chunk_id | Locator | Decision | Applicable 5B Lenses | Adjacent Context | Exclusion Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U0001 | page 1 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.7 | Document cover page — establishes source as IMF 2022 Article IV consultation, Mexico, published November 2022, authoritative international organization source. Staff report completed October 18, 2022 following discussions ending September 23, 2022. | — |
| U0002 | page 2 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Executive Board conclusion — summarizes IMF board assessment of Mexico's macroeconomic situation: fiscal deficit 3.8% GDP, gross public debt ~56% GDP, headline inflation 8.7%, monetary policy rate 9.25%, current account deficit, banking system resilient. Directly bears on fiscal/monetary rule credibility (5B.3), shock management (5B.9), and inherited trajectory assessment (5B.10). | — |
| U0003 | page 3 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.8, 5B.10 | Executive Board directors' assessment — covers: supply-side agenda for higher inclusive growth (5B.1); fiscal stance appropriateness (5B.3); financial system resilience (5B.3); governance/rule of law as growth obstacle (5B.4, 5B.5); targeted support vs untargeted subsidies (5B.8); tax reform for productive spending (5B.10); competition, energy sector private participation (5B.4). Rich direct evidence of board-level evaluation of Mexican economic governance. | — |
| U0004 | page 4 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Selected economic indicators table — GDP growth 2.1% (2022), 1.2% (2023); inflation 8.5% end-2022; fiscal balance -3.8% GDP; gross debt 56.2% GDP; unemployment 3.4%; current account -1.2% GDP. Quantitative baseline for assessing rule adherence (5B.3), distributional burden (5B.8), shock response (5B.9), and trajectory vs inherited position (5B.10). | — |
| U0005 | page 5 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.1, 5B.2, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Staff report key issues and main policy recommendations — covers: fiscal policy recommendations (market-based fuel pricing, targeted income support, productive spending financed by tax reform) (5B.1, 5B.6, 5B.8); monetary policy (restrictive rate stance) (5B.3); financial sector policies (regulatory agencies, supervision, cyber risks, macroprudential) (5B.2, 5B.5); supply-side policies (rule of law, governance, labor market formality, competition, energy sector) (5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.7). | — |
| U0006 | page 6 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3 | Staff report context and contents — lists sections including: context; recent developments; outlook and risks; policy discussions (tackling inflation, downside risks, financial system, growth); staff appraisal. Establishes document structure and analytical scope for all 5B lenses. | — |
| U0007 | page 7 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3 | Table of contents — confirms full coverage of macroeconomic policy, financial sector, and structural reform topics relevant across all 5B lenses. | — |
| U0008 | page 8 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.10 | Context section — discusses: pandemic recovery challenges; long-standing problems of low growth, weak productivity, high inequality; investment weakness; obstacles to higher inclusive growth: rule of law, corruption, crime, regional disparities, weak education/health outcomes. Directly bears on 5B.1 (prosperity agenda), 5B.4 (fair regulations), 5B.5 (corruption/governance), 5B.10 (inherited trajectory). | — |
| U0009 | page 9 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9 | Recent developments: inflation analysis — headline inflation 8.7% August 2022 (rose from 3% end-2020, 7.4% end-2021); core inflation 8.1%; energy subsidies reduced fuel inflation; food inflation 14.1% (50%+ of excess inflation above target); near-term expectations above upper target limit; medium-term expectations rising. Evidence on monetary/fiscal rule adherence (5B.3), information reliability (5B.7), and shock management (5B.9). | — |
| U0010 | page 10 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.9 | Capacity utilization, unemployment/underemployment data; Banco de México response to inflation with acceleration in pace of monetary tightening — from 25bp hikes to 50bp and 75bp hikes; policy rate 9.25% (~6pp above U.S. Fed); markets pricing terminal rate ~10.5% in Q1 2023. Direct evidence of monetary policy rule credibility (5B.3) and shock response (5B.9). | — |
| U0011 | page 11 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.9 | Financial conditions tightening — interest rates and bond yields at highest since Global Financial Crisis; real yields on inflation-linked Udibonos rising; sovereign risk spreads; portfolio outflows offset by domestic institutional investors (pension funds); peso broadly stable; gross international reserves adequate at 125% ARA metric. Evidence of macroeconomic stability rules (5B.3) and shock resilience (5B.9). | — |
| U0012 | page 12 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.9 | Credit growth recovering despite tighter conditions; bank capital adequacy >19% (up from 16% pre-pandemic); PEMEX benefiting from higher oil prices (EBITDA >$23bn H1 2022); fuel subsidies rising after Ukraine invasion; food price stabilization agreement with producers/distributors; tariff reductions on certain foods. Evidence on financial sector rules (5B.3), budget execution quality (5B.6), and shock response (5B.9). | — |
| U0013 | page 13 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Outlook and risks — growth projected 2.1% (2022), 1.2% (2023); current account to widen ~1% GDP; fiscal deficit 3.8% GDP; 2023 budget targets small deficit increase to 4.1% GDP due to interest payments; neutral fiscal stance. Evidence on fiscal rules (5B.3), budget execution (5B.6), trajectory assessment (5B.10). | — |
| U0014 | page 14 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9 | Inflation projected to plateau ~8.5% H2 2022 then decline gradually; return to 3% target midpoint by mid-2024 assuming rate rises to ~10% and maintained; risks tilted to upside; scenario analysis of global tightening and inflation (3-layer shock: commodity shock, expectations dislocation, domestic demand decline — could cause 2%+ GDP loss). Evidence on monetary rule credibility (5B.3), information/evaluation (5B.7), and shock management (5B.9). | — |

Evidence on trajectory (5B.10) and shock risks (5B.9). | — |
| U0016 | page 16 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.9, 5B.10 | Box 2: Global tightening and inflation scenario — G20MOD model simulation; three layers: (1) oil/food price shock (inflation +1% above baseline, limited output effect); (2) expectations dislocation requiring sharp rate increases (output >1% below baseline by H1 2023); (3) 1% domestic demand decline (output >2% below baseline at trough). Evidence on shock scenario analysis (5B.9) and trajectory (5B.10). | — |
| U0017 | page 17 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.2, 5B.3, 5B.7 | Monetary policy section — Banxico proactive approach to broad-based inflation; ex-ante real policy rate ~4% restrictive by September 2022; policy rate expected to reach ≥10% for inflation reversal within ~2 years; clear monetary policy communication (publication of inflation forecasts, rate guidance). Evidence on monetary rule (5B.3), information reliability (5B.7), and shock response (5B.9). | — |

Evidence on budget execution quality (5B.6), distributional fairness (5B.8), and shock response (5B.9). | — |

Evidence on information/transparency (5B.7) and shock management (5B.9). | — |
